What We Do

Full-Service Anesthesia Revenue Cycle Management

Anesthesia billing operates on a unique formula, base units plus time units multiplied by the conversion factor, with separate rules for physician anesthesiologists, CRNAs, and medically directed cases. PMEX manages the calculation, the modifier, and the concurrent case rules for every case your group does.

Base + Time Unit Billing

ASA unit value plus time units calculated per minute from the anesthesia record.

Medical Direction Billing

Modifier QK/QX/QY/QZ applied per the concurrent case supervision model.

CRNA Billing

Independent CRNA (AA modifier) and medically directed CRNA billing managed.

Anesthesia Time Verification

Start/stop times verified against the OR record before submission.

MAC Billing

Monitored anesthesia care (QS modifier) billed with correct documentation.

Pain Management Coordination

Post-op pain management codes billed separately from the anesthesia claim.

Common Anesthesia Billing Problems, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Time units miscalculated, minutes rounded incorrectly, losing 1–2 units per case.

PMEX calculates time units from verified OR start/stop times using the correct ASA rounding rule.

Medical direction modifier wrong, QK vs. QY applied incorrectly for concurrent cases.

PMEX tracks concurrent case counts per session and applies the correct modifier per actual case count.

CRNA modifier missing, AA or QX not applied, claim rejects at payer editing.

PMEX applies the correct anesthesia provider modifier on every claim before submission.

Anesthesia start/stop time not documented, time units cannot be calculated.

PMEX flags missing time documentation before billing and resolves with the OR record.

MAC billed without QS modifier, payer adjudicates at wrong rate.

PMEX confirms QS modifier application and MAC medical necessity documentation before submission.

Concurrent case limit exceeded, more than 4 cases billed under QK.

PMEX flags the 4-case medical direction limit and routes excess cases to correct supervision billing.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Anesthesia Billing, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Anesthesia practices lose 12–20% of revenue to modifier errors, time calculation mistakes, and concurrent case compliance failures.

PATTERN 01

Time Unit Calculation Error, Minutes Rounded Down

Case time: 73 minutes. Billing submits 4 units (rounded down). Correct: 5 units (round to nearest). One unit lost per case = $18–$28 per case. Across 400 monthly cases: $7,200–$11,200 per month.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX calculates anesthesia time units per case from verified start and stop times, applying the correct nearest-whole-unit rounding rule and confirming against the OR log before submission.

PATTERN 02

Medical Direction Modifier Mismatch, Wrong Concurrent Count

Anesthesiologist directing 3 concurrent CRNAs. QK applied (correct for 2–4). However a 5th case added mid-session without documentation, exceeding the 4-case limit. All 5 cases lose the direction modifier.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks concurrent case counts per anesthesiologist per session, flagging cases that exceed the 4-case medical direction limit before submission.

PATTERN 03

CRNA Claim Submitted Without Modifier, Rejected at Editing

CRNA performs case independently. Claim submitted without AA modifier. Claim rejects at clearinghouse, anesthesia claims require a provider modifier. Revenue delayed while correction is pending.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies AA (physician/independent CRNA), QX (directed CRNA), or QZ (opt-out CRNA) on every claim, confirmed before submission.

Anesthesia Billing Questions Answered

From anesthesia start time (when preparation begins) to stop time (patient transferred to PACU), divided by 15 minutes per unit, rounded to the nearest whole unit per ASA guidelines.

Medical direction (QK/QX) applies when an anesthesiologist directs 2–4 concurrent CRNAs and meets the 7 CMS requirements. Medical supervision (QY) applies when directing more than 4 concurrent cases.

In medically directed cases, the anesthesiologist bills QK and the CRNA bills QX, each at 50% of the allowed amount. We manage both claims together.

MAC is billed with the QS modifier. Documentation must support clinical need for the anesthesiologist's presence. We confirm modifier application and medical necessity before submission.
